review_notes: I read the whole file, lines 1–307. It has no @[simp] declarations, no simp-normal-form questions, no orientation choices and no rewrite equations. The declarations are relation definitions (SubdivisionStep, Subdivides, HasCommonSubdivision, MoveEquivalent), closure lemmas such as refl, trans and symm, and implication-style preservation theorems. The preservation lemmas are hypothesis-to-conclusion implications, not equalities. They are not suitable simp lemmas, and tagging them would risk unwanted side-condition search. The relations are not reducible. I found no rewrite cycle or competing rule. I did one grep over the ClassificationOfSurfaces directory for simp, refl, symm and trans attributes and for uses of these names. I did not read the individual hits, so I can't rule out a downstream use that would justify an attribute. The rubric tells me not to recommend simp attributes just because an identity looks simple, and I found nothing concrete beyond that.
